review_notes: I read the whole file and the upstream definitions in SphereConeChart.lean, SchwarzschildModel.lean and SphereConeMeasure.lean. I grepped for uses of sphereCone, join_zero, drop_join and sphereParam_norm across the repo. The file has no simp attributes of its own. The two findings concern its simp interface: the `sphereCone` definition is unfolded by hand, and `sphereParam_norm` is passed by name. I did not run Lean. Whether the proposed lemmas would work as simp lemmas is untested, and the suggested statements need checking against the actual definitions. `join_zero` and `drop_join` are already @[simp], so the rewriting of their targets is fine.

findings.problem: There is no simp lemma for `sphereCone` applied to `join (r,y)`. Each proof unfolds the definition and then replays `join_zero` and `drop_join` by hand. This happens at lines 16 and 40, and line 34 uses `simp [sphereCone]`. `sphereCone` is a plain `def`, so unfolding it is the only route, and it exposes the internal form `(z 0) • sphereParam p (dropPlane z)` to every caller. The same unfold-and-replay pattern appears in `sphereCone_hasFDerivAt` and `SphereConeMeasure`, whose proofs also call `join_zero`/`drop_join` by name.
findings.proposed_change: In SphereConeChart.lean, next to `sphereCone`, add `@[simp] lemma sphereCone_join (p : Sphere) (z : ℝ × E2) : sphereCone p (join z) = z.1 • sphereParam p z.2`. Its proof would be `by simp [sphereCone]`. Optionally also add `sphereCone_apply_zero`. Then replace the three unfold calls with `simp only [sphereCone_join]` or plain `simp`.
findings.benefit: Callers get a stable normal form `r • sphereParam p y` without unfolding `sphereCone`. The three proofs become shorter and no longer depend on the definition's internal shape.

evidence.excerpt: def sphereCone (p : Sphere) (z : E3) : E3 := (z 0) • sphereParam p (dropPlane z)
@[simp] lemma drop_join (z : ℝ × E2) : dropPlane (join z) = z.2 := by ext i; rfl

findings.declaration: sphereCone_injOn (use of `sphereParam_norm` as an explicit simp argument)
findings.excerpt: simp only [norm_smul,sphereParam_norm,mul_one,Real.norm_eq_abs,abs_of_pos hr.1,abs_of_pos ht.1] at hn
findings.problem: `sphereParam_norm : ‖sphereParam p y‖ = 1` is not tagged @[simp]. Any `simp` that meets `‖sphereParam p y‖` will not reduce it to 1. Callers have to pass the lemma by name, as here. The same happens in TailEnergy.lean, which passes it to `rw`, to `simpa only` and to other lemmas. The statement is a canonical rewrite with LHS-to-literal orientation and no hypotheses, so it cannot loop. It is a good simp-lemma candidate because `sphereParam` is a def that simp cannot see through. Without the attribute, `norm_smul` followed by `simp` leaves `‖sphereParam p y‖` unsimplified.
findings.proposed_change: Mark the lemma `@[simp] lemma sphereParam_norm ...` in SphereConeChart.lean. The statement is unchanged. Then shorten line 18 to `simp only [norm_smul, sphereParam_norm, ...]` or plain `simp [abs_of_pos hr.1, abs_of_pos ht.1]`, and drop the explicit argument at other call sites where possible.
findings.benefit: Norm computations involving `sphereParam` normalise to 1 automatically. That removes the manual `sphereParam_norm` arguments in downstream cone and tensor proofs.

evidence.excerpt: lemma sphereParam_norm (p : Sphere) (y : E2) : ‖sphereParam p y‖ = 1 := by
